ground_truth.title: Mailchimp Alternatives: Top 15 Options for 2026 (some are even free!)
ground_truth.author: Inka Wibowo
ground_truth.main_content:
🤔 Tired of biased articles written by email service providers themselves?

We get it; they always want to sell you their own service. That's why we wrote this guide – to give you an honest overview of Mailchimp's competitors.

There was once a time when Mailchimp was the first name that came to mind when you thought about ESPs (email service providers).

The marketing platform was a breath of fresh air within the email marketing industry. With its affordable pricing model and ease of use, it was a big hit with small-to-medium businesses, bloggers, online store owners, and other smaller-scale users.

But with constant changes to their pricing model (and increased restrictions to their freemium plan), more and more users are canceling their accounts and seeking Mailchimp alternatives.

So if you’re one of those users, or would simply like to know what other comparable tools are out there, read on to find out which Mailchimp alternative is right for you.

After extensive testing, we've found that the following email marketing services are the best Mailchimp competitors. Keep scrolling for a detailed breakdown.

MailerLite – Same quality but cheaper

Brevo (formerly Sendinblue)- Better email automation and cheaper

Omnisend – Ideal for ecommerce

GetResponse – More features

Moosend – Generous on features and emails

ActiveCampaign – Better marketing automation

EmailOctopus – Very affordable

EngageBay – Excellent CRM features

Zoho – Myriad of automations

Hubspot – All-in-one CRM platform

Mailjet – Affordable but basic

Kit – Better targeting

Beehiiv – Monetize your newsletter

Benchmark – Multilingual teams

AWeber – Better support

If you don't have time to read the whole article right now, check out our 5-minute video, which summarizes the main points:

Or, you could also answer the 6 questions in the quiz below to find a personalized Mailchimp alternative recommendation:

Smart Quiz: Find the Best Mailchimp Alternative in 1 Minute

An Overview of The Top Mailchimp Competitors

Email Marketing Service Ease of use Price Features
Omnisend Full review SPONSORED Their interface is simple, and they have a fresh and speedy email builder that’s similar to Mailchimp’s. Free version available Paid plans start at $16 per month Try for free Marketing automations specific to ecommerce – web tracking, abandoned cart, order confirmations, etc. Plus, some cool interactive features like scratch cards and gift boxes for maximizing conversions.
MailerLite Full review Excellent email builder – fast and logical. Good support too. Free plan available Paid plans start at $25 per month Try for free They offer email marketing automation, a landing page builder and reporting – not as powerful as other solutions, but available for free and/or much cheaper.
Brevo (Sendinblue) Full review Easy to navigate software that guides you through the production flow. Free version available Paid plans start at $9 per month Try for free Pretty good marketing automation and contact management. Very affordable prices. Reporting and analytics aren’t as good as Mailchimp’s.
GetResponse Full review Very easy to use. Their knowledge base is a bit confusing though. Free version available Paid plans start at $19 per month Try for free Powerful marketing automation workflows and list management. Interesting extras such as a mobile app, landing page builder and webinar creator. Not so good for analytics and reports.
Moosend Full review Fairly straightforward to use. Live chat support available within the drag and drop email builder. Paid plans start at $9 per month Try for free Very affordable email marketing service with unlimited emails. Freemium plan was removed. Email deliverability isn't as good as Mailchimp’s.
ActiveCampaign Full review Fairly easy. Even if it seems more overwhelming, the support and wizards are very good. From $19 per month Try for free Very powerful sales and marketing automation. A/B tests, timed automations, CRM, landing page editor and much more. Good contact management. The reporting is good, but not as powerful as Mailchimp’s.
EmailOctopus Full review One of the most affordable and beginner-friendly email marketing tools out there. Paid plans start at $10 per month Try for free Very affordable email marketing service. Focus on deliverability, with list cleaning and full authentication support. However, it lacks Mailchimp’s advanced automation, deeper analytics, and wider integrations.
EngageBay Full review The interface is well-designed, making it a very easy-to-use tool. Free version available Paid plans start from $12.99/month Try for free Generous free plan and affordable paid plans. Excellent email marketing software and CRM features.
Zoho Pretty easy to use. Live chat support available within the email builder. Free version available Paid plans start at $5 per month Try for free Generous free plan. Advanced email marketing automation and segmentation.
Hubspot Very easy to navigate. Users can create content such as landing pages, emails, and forms with a drag-and-drop builder. Free version available Paid plans start from $50 Try for free They offer free email marketing and CRM software with unlimited users. Customer support is available. Access to omnichannel marketing once upgraded. Basic templates on offer.
Mailjet Full review Setting up email newsletters and contact lists is easy to do! Free version available Paid plans start at $17 per month Offers affordable prices and great collaboration features. Good choice for transactional emails. Basic marketing automation.
Kit Full review Automations are easier to use than average. Other features, like creating forms, can be overcomplicated. Free version available Paid plans start at $15 per month Try for free Good automations, monetization, and list segmentation functionalities. Newsletter and landing page design and reporting should be improved.
Beehiiv Full review Clean and intuitive dashboard designed specifically for newsletter creators, making it easy to write, publish, and manage emails without unnecessary complexity. Free version available Paid plans start at $49 per month Try for free Built-in monetization tools allow creators to easily set up paid subscriptions, sponsorships, and referral programs. But its lack of pre-designed templates can be a challenge for those without design experience.
Benchmark Full review Very good email builder and outstanding support. Free version available Paid plans start at $0 per month Try for free Good for multi-languages. Not great for marketing automation, and the file storage charges are an extra worry. Historically, have not performed so well in our deliverability tests.
AWeber Full review Some sections are a little hidden, and you'll need to make sure you're in the right email list at all times. Their terminology could be confusing for experienced users. Free version available Paid plans start at $15 per month Try for free Very good support and list and subscriber management features. Sales tracking available for your site.
For comparison: Mailchimp Full review Very easy. The email builder is great for beginners, and the paid email templates also look good. Paid plans start at $13 per month Great for reports and decent ecommerce integration. Not so good for list segmentation, and paid plans get pricey quickly. Unfair subscriber count (unlike with other ESPs, you pay for unsubscribed and bounced users).

The Best Mailchimp Alternatives

1. MailerLite

Our favorite alternative to Mailchimp is MailerLite. We have used MailerLite for our own newsletters and automated emails here at EmailTooltester, and love how easy they make it to run our email marketing on autopilot.

This relatively young Lithuanian email marketing service prides itself on its modern and sleek aesthetic, which really comes through in their eye-catching website and easy-to-navigate platform.

Like Mailchimp, MailerLite are also beginning to incorporate AI email marketing tools into their offering, including an email AI writing assistant to help you whip up emails, subject lines, and calls-to-action with just a few prompts.

They also offer good multilingual options as well as a decent free plan. If you're looking for awesome email and landing page designs, MailerLite really shines in this area (although one drawback is that templates are not available on free plan).

Where MailerLite is better than Mailchimp:

The free plan, which comes with 500 subscribers and 12,000 emails, is much more generous than Mailchimp's freemium plan. Plus, MailerLite's paid plans are significantly cheaper, making them a great choice for small businesses on a tight marketing budget.

We find MailerLite's platform easier to use than Mailchimp's. It includes a number of features, including a landing page editor that, in our opinion, is better than what Mailchimp offers. They also have an app for iOS, and a website builder. So, there are a lot of great features packed into this very affordable tool!

Finally, if you want to work in your native tongue, they offer 5 languages. There are plenty of reasons why Mailchimp users migrate to Mailerlite.

> See how the two marketing tools compare in our MailerLite vs Mailchimp guide, and check out other MailerLite alternatives.

Where Mailchimp is better than MailerLite:

MailerLite falls short when it comes to its reporting and tracking tools (no social tracking), which makes it less than ideal for optimizing your campaigns. Mailchimp does a better job in this area.

It's also lacking more advanced automations, such as being able to send email campaigns based on webpage visits. If you're after this level of targeting, we'd recommend Mailchimp alternatives like Brevo, ActiveCampaign or GetResponse (which we talk about below).

Try MailerLite for free

2. Brevo (formerly Sendinblue)

If you're looking for a very affordable Mailchimp alternative, we'd recommend checking out the newsletter service that was previously known as Sendinblue. Brevo is a Paris-based company who has decided to make waves by offering some of the cheapest plans available.

And they’re also surprisingly good when it comes to marketing automation workflows and list management. Plus, they can be used to send transactional emails and SMS marketing.

Check out our detailed Brevo vs Mailchimp comparison to find out more about why Brevo is a great Mailchimp alternative, or watch our video:

Where Brevo is better than Mailchimp:

Brevo is cheaper than Mailchimp. Their automation workflows system is a little more advanced, allowing you to A/B test a number of components.

EU-based customers will love the fact that their servers are located in Germany. You can also send SMS at a very reasonable price. Mailchimp requires you to set up an online store with them in order to send SMS.

> See how the email marketing tools compare in our Brevo vs Mailchimp guide.

Where Mailchimp is better than Brevo:

Mailchimp's email builder beats Brevo’s, and not many companies can top their social media tracking for accurate reports.

We've also found that Brevo's deliverability rates can fluctuate, which is a little worrying. Mailchimp tend to offer better deliverability on average.

Try Brevo for free

3. Omnisend

Another great Mailchimp alternative is Omnisend. This is an email and SMS platform with a strong slant toward ecommerce – something that shines through in their conversion-focused automation and segmentation options. And while Mailchimp does a decent job of ecommerce, there are some clever little extras that we think give Omnisend the one up here, as you'll see in a second.

Omnisend integrates really well with Shopify. You can also use it with the following ecommerce platforms: BigCommerce, WooCommerce, Volusion, PrestaShop and Magento.

Where Omnisend is better than Mailchimp:

Like Mailchimp, Omnisend offers stacks of automations for online stores, including browse abandonment and cart recovery (these are editable through visual workflows).

But it goes a step further with unique features like ‘wheel of fortune’ incentives for sign-ups, interactive gift boxes, automated product recommendations, and even ‘live view’ website tracking – powerful tools for your ecommerce email marketing strategy (and ones that we haven't seen being offered elsewhere).

You can also segment your email lists based on very granular data, including customers who purchased a specific product or used a discount code.

Another point in Omnisend’s favor: it also includes some very modern landing page templates, and SMS marketing is included for free.

> See how the email marketing tools compare in our Omnisend vs Mailchimp guide.

Where Mailchimp is better than Omnisend:

Outside of ecommerce, Mailchimp is probably the more versatile tool, offering more options for email templates and automation. Mailchimp also includes a higher sending allowance on its free plan.

Finally, we found Omnisend had one of the lowest deliverability rates among the tools we've tested – something you should keep a close eye on if you decide to go with them.

Try Omnisend for free

4. GetResponse

One of the most powerful platforms we've found when it comes to marketing automation, GetResponse offers a wide range of unique pro features such as a landing page creator and a webinar tool.

They also claim to be one of the easiest email newsletter tools available and give you loads of extra tidbits like access to free iStock photo images, and an iOS and Android app to send your campaigns on the go.

But would we say they're better than Mailchimp? In most cases, yes!

Where GetResponse is better than Mailchimp:

What makes GetResponse a worthy alternative to Mailchimp? For one thing, its email marketing automation is very powerful, letting you trigger sales actions, A/B tests, and segment removal, amongst other things. For example, you can use automations to easily move subscribers between lists (e.g. “prospect” to “customer”).

It also offers features that we haven't found in any other email marketing platform. These include the ability to create and run webinars, and the Conversion funnel feature, which facilitates setting up sales funnels. (Find out more about their sales funnel software here.)

If you’re an international team, you will appreciate the 25 languages available in the interface.

Finally, their multimedia center, which lets you access stock photos and generate QR codes, amongst others, is also a nice extra.

> See how the marketing tools compare in our GetResponse vs Mailchimp guide.

Where Mailchimp is better than GetResponse:

GetResponse’s analytics don't go as deep as Mailchimp’s. For example, it lacks click heatmaps (to let you see which links/images/calls-t0-action are most effective in driving clicks).

Features such as contact tagging and abandoned cart emails are reserved for the more expensive Plus plan, whereas Mailchimp offers these features on their free plan.

In addition to this, GetResponse limits the number of files (e.g. images) that you can store in their media center to 1 GB, while Mailchimp doesn’t.

Check out our GetResponse vs Mailchimp guide for more information. Or try GetResponse for free.

5. Moosend

Moosend might not be as well known as some of the other Mailchimp alternatives on this list, but they caught our eye for their affordable prices, good selection of responsive email templates, and advanced segmentation.

What's more, they have excellent marketing automation features, including a range of ready-to-go templates and an intuitive workflow editor.

Where Moosend is better than Mailchimp:

All emails are ad-free and we've found their paid plans to be pretty affordable. Plans start at just $9 per month and even if you have a larger list, you won't be paying a fortune (at $88/month for 10,000 subscribers, they are significantly cheaper than Mailchimp).

Advanced segmentation, landing pages and a well-designed visual automation builder are all included.

Where Mailchimp is better than Moosend:

Moosend’s deliverability could do with some improvement, and we would recommend keeping a close eye on campaign performance rates and doing all you can to boost your deliverability.

When it comes to native integrations, Mailchimp also offers quite a bit more than Moosend. Moosend only includes direct integrations with a handful of tools, although these can be extended through its Zapier integration.

Try Moosend for free!

6. ActiveCampaign

This self-described “all-in-one marketing platform” is focused on letting you reach your email marketing goals with fewer emails. To that end, ActiveCampaign offer some of the best marketing automation features we’ve ever tested, making them a great alternative to Mailchimp.

You can easily create very complex sequences of emails and add a huge number of parameters such as “wait x number of days before sending”, “split test between two messages” and much more.

The fact that all plans come with unlimited emails is pretty attractive, too.

But would we say they're better than Mailchimp? Read on to find out.

Where ActiveCampaign is better than Mailchimp:

In terms of email sequences automation, ActiveCampaign is unbeatable. Whether you want to tag users based on behavior, run A/B tests or create complex timed automations, they have you covered.

Their CRM system is robust, and they are often launching interesting features such as live chat for your website, and “site messages”, which lets you create personalized content on your website, and landing pages when for capturing subscribers or running lead magnet campaigns.

List management, which Mailchimp isn’t great at, is also a strong suit, as you can set up complex segmentation automation.

Its white labeling features and Agency Reseller Program also make it a much more complete option for agencies serving multiple clients.

Finally, despite being one of the pricier platforms on this list, they also end up cheaper than Mailchimp, and the customer support you get in return is excellent.

> See how the email marketing tools compare in our ActiveCampaign vs Mailchimp guide.

> You might also want to check out our ActiveCampaign vs GetResponse guide.

Where Mailchimp is better than ActiveCampaign:

Given the huge range of features on offer, it's not surprising that ActiveCampaign isn't exactly what we'd call beginner-friendly. It's quicker and easier to get up and running with Mailchimp, although we do have to give ActiveCampaign kudos for their ample support resources.

One thing to note is that ActiveCampaign doesn’t offer a free plan, which means you'll have to pay to keep using it after your 14-day trial is up.

We also found Mailchimp’s ecommerce tracking to be more robust (ActiveCampaign offers purchase tracking only for Shopify, BigCommerce and WooCommerce). Also, ActiveCampaign's integration with WooCommerce is only available to users on the Plus plan (from $70) and above, whereas Mailchimp offer this integration for free – something to keep in mind if you have a WooCommerce store.

Discover other great alternatives to ActiveCampaign here.

Try ActiveCampaign for free

7. EmailOctopus

EmailOctopus is a lightweight, budget-friendly email marketing tool that focuses on helping users create simple newsletters and straightforward automation without unnecessary complexity. It has become a popular choice for bloggers, nonprofits, small businesses, and creators who want a clean interface, reliable deliverability, and low pricing.

While Mailchimp offers a wider range of advanced features, EmailOctopus stands out for its simplicity, affordability, and ease of use. Let’s take a closer look at how it compares.

Where EmailOctopus is better than Mailchimp:

Much more affordable, especially as your list grows. EmailOctopus’ pricing remains low even at higher subscriber counts.

Cleaner, more intuitive interface, which makes creating newsletters and basic automations quick and beginner-friendly.

More generous free plan for anyone starting a newsletter or small project.

Better focus on deliverability; offering list cleaning services, full authentication setup, and they even manually review emails and automations before you can activate them.

Data hosted on servers located in the European Union (important for GDPR compliance).

Where Mailchimp is better than EmailOctopus:

Far more advanced automation options for multi-step or behaviour-based workflows.

Better native integrations, especially for ecommerce platforms and CRMs.

More polished email and landing page editors with richer customisation.

Deeper reporting and analytics, including comparative benchmarks and customer journey insights.

Additional features like multivariate testing, predictive segments and advanced scheduling, which EmailOctopus doesn’t offer.

Try EmailOctopus for free

8. EngageBay

Although a relatively new product in the marketing automation niche, EngageBay has quickly grown in popularity as one of the most affordable all-in-one CRMs.

EngageBay is a great Mailchimp alternative due to the myriad of tools for email marketing, email and workflow automation, customer service management and social media management.

To our surprise, EngageBay's free plan is loaded with features that other platforms offer only with paid plans, which gives us good chance to see just how it compares against Mailchimp.

Where EngageBay is better than Mailchimp:

Mailchimp gets expensive pretty fast. Their sliding scale pricing structure can look affordable at first. But as your contact list starts growing, so will the price you pay.

By contrast, EngageBay offers a lot better value for money. For example, EngageBay’s Marketing Bay allows for up to 30,000 contacts at $49.99. To get the same number of contacts on Mailchimp, you have to pay a jaw-dropping $219! If you want all the pro features, you have to purchase the Premium plan. The cost? A whopping $499 a month!

What we found disappointing is that Mailchimp doesn’t even reward its loyal customers. EngageBay, on the other hand, offers a 20% discount on annual subscriptions and a 40% discount on biennial subscriptions. This brings the already affordable costs even further down.

Plus, EngageBay's free plan comes with email and chat support, which is a real disadvantage to using Mailchimp as they only offer a chatbot and email support on their free plan.

In terms of the CRM features, you’ll have a separate dashboard for marketing, sales and service, which keeps everything manageable. You’ll also have an area for ‘deals’, which is great for small businesses who want to keep everything under one roof. Mailchimp doesn’t offer pipeline management or much in the way of CRM features.

If you need a robust and affordable all-in-one marketing tool, then we’d recommend EngageBay.

Where Mailchimp is better than EngageBay:

Mailchimp has a dedicated desktop application for both Windows and Mac. It offers search marketing (SEO and PPC with Facebook, Google and Instagram), which EngageBay doesn't.

You can also set up single-step automations with Mailchimp’s free plan, whereas EngageBay reserves marketing automation workflows for those who sign up to the Growth plan (which starts at $24.99/month).

Try EngageBay for free

9. Zoho Campaigns

Zoho offers an impressive suite of services, which of course includes email marketing. We've always been impressed by their ever-growing product range, which goes beyond sales and marketing tools to include helpdesk software, online conferencing, project management and collaboration tools.

Considering how much ground they cover, and the fact that they offer a free plan, Zoho is a comprehensive Mailchimp alternative that could be very well suited to your small business needs.

Where Zoho is better than Mailchimp:

A cool feature from Zoho is that you can insert images from Unsplash directly in the email builder. We also liked their range of email and form templates.

Zoho excels in the area of automation; they offer workflows for nurturing, ecommerce, re-engagement, and more.

What’s more, because Zoho comes with powerful CRM software, you can set up workflows to help you move leads through your sales funnel.

List segmentation is a simple affair, with plenty of segmentation options that let you create segments based on contact activities, campaign registrations, lead scores, tags, and more.

Where Mailchimp is better than Zoho:

Though Zoho has a fair amount, Mailchimp still beats them when it comes to native integrations, with over 250 compared to Zoho's more modest range of 60.

We also find that Mailchimp is still a more intuitive marketing platform for beginners, as Zoho's interface design isn’t the most user-friendly, and can also be sluggish at times.

Try Zoho Campaigns for free!

Or, learn more about how it compares to Mailchimp in our Zoho Campaigns vs Mailchimp comparison.

10. HubSpot

Branded as an all-in-one CRM platform, HubSpot is a powerful alternative to Mailchimp for both sales and marketing teams.

With such an extensive number of features spread across 5 ‘hubs', HubSpot helps businesses grow with their crafted marketing, sales, and customer service solutions. The hubs are available through 5 stand-alone products; Marketing Hub, Sales Hub, Service Hub, Operations Hub, and CMS Hub, which can also be bundled together at an extra cost.

Alternatively, HubSpot offers a selection of free tools, which are “lite” versions of their paid products.

From contact management, live chat, SEO, and sales playbooks to help desk tools, HubSpot offers an impressive full-service digital marketing and email platform for the modern-day marketer.

Where HubSpot is better than Mailchimp:

On the whole, HubSpot and Mailchimp both offer similar capabilities through their tools and features. However, HubSpot offers them on a much more comprehensive level.

In terms of email automation, reports and analytics, HubSpot gives users access to a wider variety of automation features and a much more robust built-in CRM.

If you're looking for a solution to manage your email marketing, deals and contacts under one roof, HubSpot is better than Mailchimp.

Where Mailchimp is better than HubSpot:

Generally speaking, Mailchimp is cheaper than HubSpot, although it shares many of the same features and functionalities ( see HubSpot’s pricing ).

If you are a smaller company, searching for an easy and reasonably-priced email marketing platform, Mailchimp is for you.

Mailchimp provides a variety of features designed for small business owners to help grow your business in its early stages.

Watch our Hubspot vs Mailchimp video review:

Try HubSpot for free

11. Mailjet

Mailjet, a French email service provider, is one of the more affordable email marketing tool on the market, making it an interesting Mailchimp alternative!

A neat feature is that the drag and drop email editor allows you to collaborate with other team members in real-time. This can make the design process much more agile, leading to better-performing campaigns (so long as it doesn’t become a “too-many-cooks” situation!).

Where Mailjet is better than Mailchimp:

Making sure your emails are delivered to your subscribers is crucial, and Mailjet definitely has an edge over Mailchimp in this area. Our recent deliverability tests show that Mailjet takes this very seriously, keeping their scores up in the mid-nineties. This also makes them a great choice for sending transactional emails via SMTP.

Another big plus for Mailjet is the price. Aside from offering a free plan with up to 200 emails per day and no contact limit, their paid plans are also some of the most affordable on the market.

Mailjet’s Premium plan ($25/month) allows you to send up to 15,000 emails/month to unlimited contacts and benefit from all its features. By comparison, Mailchimp’s similarly-priced Essentials plan (which has more or less the same features) will limit you to 1,500 contacts.

See how Mailchimp and Mailjet compare in this side-by-side table.

Where Mailchimp is better than Mailjet:

It’s not necessarily where Mailchimp wins, but more where Mailjet slightly disappoints: the automations. These are limited to date-based and contact field conditions and are missing more behavioral triggers such as ‘has opened X email’ or ‘has clicked X link’.

As a whole, Mailchimp does a better job at automations. Of course, if you’re serious about marketing automation then we’d recommend ActiveCampaign or GetResponse.

12. Kit

Designed with digital marketing needs in mind, Kit has become popular with content creators and bloggers looking to connect with their audiences through email marketing. They offer nifty features such as a Content Creator network (which helps you get more subscribers through recommendations from other content creators), and monetization tools such as a tip jar, and the ability to sell digital products through the platform.

Generally speaking, Mailchimp is the more well-rounded tool, but let’s check this in more detail to see if Kit make a good Mailchimp alternative.

Where Kit is better than Mailchimp:

Managing lists and contacts is more flexible, allowing you to easily tag contacts and create better targeted email marketing campaigns.

You can use a custom domain name for landing pages even on the free plan, which is a big plus.

They also have responsive support, which can be an issue with Mailchimp.

> See how the tools compare in our Kit vs Mailchimp guide.

Where Mailchimp is better than Kit:

Mailchimp's free plan offers more advanced features such as third-party integrations, deep reporting, and more.

Mailchimp's email and landing page editors are also really flexible – Kit’s simplistic editors and templates don't even compare.

With Mailchimp, you can create users for several team members, which is unfortunately not available with Kit.

Reporting is also something Mailchimp does a lot better than Kit, whose reports are limited to open rates, click rates, unsubscribes and links clicked.

Try Kit for free

13. Beehiiv

If Kit’s content creator focus caught your attention, but you’re looking for something even more newsletter-centric, Beehiiv might be the better fit. Designed specifically for independent writers and media brands, Beehiiv offers powerful audience growth and monetization tools that go beyond what Kit or Mailchimp provide.

Key features include Boosts, a referral marketplace that helps you grow your audience through paid promotions, and monetization tools that let you set up paid subscriptions and integrate newsletter sponsorships — all within the platform.

While Mailchimp is a more established all-in-one solution, let’s see how Beehiiv compares as a Mailchimp alternative.

Where Beehiiv is better than Mailchimp:

Beehiiv is built specifically for newsletters, offering an intuitive editor and a streamlined publishing workflow that makes it easy for creators to focus on writing and audience engagement. The platform also excels in monetization, making it simple to generate revenue through paid subscriptions, sponsorships, and referral programs.

Unlike Mailchimp, which limits free users to 500 subscribers, Beehiiv’s free plan allows up to 2,500 subscribers, making it a more cost-effective option for new and growing newsletter creators.

> See how the tools compare in our Beehiiv vs Mailchimp guide.

Where Mailchimp is better than Beehiiv:

Mailchimp’s automation tools are more advanced, offering sophisticated customer journey mapping and segmentation that go beyond Beehiiv’s simpler workflows.

When it comes to design, Mailchimp provides a wide range of email templates, whereas Beehiiv requires users to create their own from scratch.

Finally, Mailchimp’s extensive integration library, which includes over 250 third-party apps, gives businesses more flexibility. Beehiiv’s integration options are still relatively limited.

Try Beehiiv for free

14. Benchmark

Is Benchmark a good Mailchimp alternative? Focusing on international markets with a presence in 15 countries around the world, Benchmark’s paid plans place them in the middle-to-high end compared to other email marketing software.

Unfortunately, their advanced features aren’t as impressive as others, but they are worth considering for their free plan.

Where Benchmark is better than Mailchimp:

Benchmark's free plan sending limit is much more generous than Mailchimp's, letting you send 3,500 emails per month (Mailchimp restricts this to just 1,000). They are a much better choice for multilingual teams, and also offer good support.

> See how Benchmark stacks up against Mailchimp in this side-by-side comparison.

Where Mailchimp is better than Benchmark:

As soon as you look at advanced features like reporting and automation, Benchmark ranks lower on our list.

They also give you very limited amounts of image data storage – which is unlimited with Mailchimp.

Try Benchmark for free

15. AWeber

AWeber has been on the email marketing scene for over 20 years, just a few years more than Mailchimp. However, it was only recently that AWeber updated its service, which now includes a freemium plan.

The free plan, though it includes the same features as the paid plan, limits you to just 500 subscribers, which isn’t many at all, though you’ll be able to send them up to 3,000 emails/month – that’s 6 emails per subscriber per month.

Features include A/B testing, email analytics and conversion tracking. They also have various mobile apps, so you can send emails on-the-go.

Where AWeber is better than Mailchimp:

AWeber’s list segmentation features help you keep your contacts organized.

You can use their automations to automatically manage subscribers via the rules you create.

They also have decent support and educational tools.

> See how the tools compare in our Aweber vs Mailchimp guide.

Where Mailchimp is better than AWeber:

We find that Mailchimp has a lot more to offer than AWeber, in terms of selection and functionality. For instance, you can even run your Facebook ad campaigns directly from your Mailchimp account.

Find out how AWeber compares to Mailchimp in this side-by-side comparison.

Of all the alternatives to Mailchimp, AWeber might not be your no. 1 choice.

Try AWeber for free

Why we don’t recommend Constant Contact

Constant Contact is, seemingly, Mailchimp’s biggest competitor. It’s been around for almost three decades and owns the second-largest share of the email marketing market (5.08%) after Mailchimp (72.69%).

However, with no free plan, high prices, and a lack of advanced features, we really struggle to recommend Constant Contact against the competition. Much like Mailchimp, it feels dated in key areas while still charging a premium, which makes it just as tricky to recommend today. Instead, we think that the email marketing services listed above provide much better value for money.

And if you’d like to explore why further, you can check out our Constant Contact alternatives post. We also have a detailed comparison of Mailchimp & Constant Contact that you may want to check out.

Free Mailchimp Alternatives

Most of the email marketing tools on the list offer a free version but of course, some are better than others.

Kit has the most generous free email marketing plan, allowing for up to 10,000 subscribers and unlimited emails. What's great is that you'll also have access to landing pages, although you're restricted to a single email sequence/automation.

MailerLite's free plan does include automations, though you're limited to 1,000 contacts and 12,000 monthly email sends.

Brevo also offers a free version, but you're limited to 300 emails/day, which isn't ideal.

The best free email marketing service for ecommerce is Omnisend, which includes all pro features on the free version. Another great ecommerce alternative is Klaviyo – you can compare Klaviyo vs Mailchimp in our complete guide.

Why Use Mailchimp?

Is there any reason that you should stick with Mailchimp?

Here's a quick summary of Mailchimp's Pros and Cons:

Mailchimp Pros

Excellent reports

Fast, easy-to-use email editor

Freemium plan

Mailchimp Cons

Expensive paid plans

Missing advanced automation features

Poor list management

Basic landing pages

Basic CRM features

Very low contact and sending limits on free plan

And despite its recent less-than-ideal changes, moving away from Mailchimp might not be the best move if:

You need detailed reporting

Mailchimp has one of the most detailed reporting systems for tracking your newsletters’ performance, offering robust options such as Google Analytics integration, Geotracking, Social media and click maps.

You have a very small email list (and I mean really small!)

Mailchimp’s pricing model imposes new limits on their free plan. Now, you are limited to only 250 contacts. If you know your total contact count will be less than this, then Mailchimp’s free plan has a pretty good selection of features available.

You want to easily design good-looking emails

Their drag and drop email builder is fast, simple and drag and drop. It’s very easy to create stunning emails that will stand out from the rest and engage your audience. They also have plenty of modern, well-designed email templates (though be aware that the templates available for free are very limited and not very modern-looking).

When Should You Look For Mailchimp Alternatives?

If you're looking for a Mailchimp alternative, make a list of the reasons why, as these won't be the same for everyone. We've analyzed the areas in which Mailchimp doesn't do so well and listed a number of Mailchimp alternatives below.

You are on a tight budget

As soon as you leave the freemium plan, things quickly start to add up at Mailchimp, especially now that they charge based on total number of contacts, rather than just subscribed contacts. Working out how much your email newsletter service will cost is not always straightforward. For instance, some will make you pay depending on the number of emails you send, others on your amount of subscribers. Luckily, we’ve created a handy cost calculator to help you get a clearer idea.

Cheaper Mailchimp alternatives: MailerLite, Brevo, Moosend, EngageBay or Mailjet

You need complex email marketing automation

If you are really aiming to get the most from your email marketing campaigns, be aware that Mailchimp offers no email marketing automation features on the free plan. That’s a huge disadvantage, especially compared to its more generous competitors. If you need campaigns based on user behavior (e.g. on your website), split tests and advanced workflows, you might want to look elsewhere.

Learn more about why we don't recommend Mailchimp for automation in our video:

Mailchimp alternatives for automations: ActiveCampaign, GetResponse

You want to manage multiple mailing lists

Because Mailchimp keeps every contact list isolated from each other, it limits the amount of flexibility, creativity and precision you can have for your complex email marketing campaigns. For example, if user X belongs to 2 of your mailing lists, they will appear as subscribers twice. There is no good way to merge lists or create interdependencies between them.

Mailchimp alternatives for multiple lists: ActiveCampaign, Brevo, Omnisend

You want to set up dynamic landing pages and A/B test them

Some email marketers do like to create special pages to send users once they click a certain link. These pages can offer tailored content and act as a powerful sales funnel or segmentation tool. Mailchimp's landing pages are a bit basic, not offering A/B testing or personalized dynamic content.

Mailchimp alternatives for landing pages: GetResponse, ActiveCampaign, MailerLite, Omnisend

You need a robust yet affordable CRM software

Collecting subscribers is one thing, but managing clients, companies and deals is quite another. As you probably know, things can get messy quickly if you don’t have a good sales and marketing tool to help you manage these processes, and keeping all your marketing and sales contacts in one place will save you a ton of time. Though Mailchimp claims to offer CRM features, these just scratch the surface, and no pipeline management features are included.

Mailchimp alternatives for CRM software: EngageBay, ActiveCampaign, Brevo, Zoho

You need strong data privacy

Mailchimp isn't the most data protection-conscious company. For example, a short while back they suddenly announced that they are about to deactivate the double opt-in feature for all customers. After an outcry from (mainly) EU-based customers, they retracted the change. Customers from Europe also usually prefer to have their data stored inside an EU country, which Mailchimp doesn't offer.

Mailchimp alternatives: Brevo, MailerLite

Note: In September 2021, Mailchimp was bought by financial software company Intuit for the sum of $12 billion. Since then, Mailchimp's pricing plans have gone through some changes – find out more in our Mailchimp pricing guide.

Mailchimp Alternatives: Conclusion

While Mailchimp was once the #1 choice when it came to a cost-effective email marketing service, a few recent pricing changes have made it a lot less affordable than it once was. There are alternatives to Mailchimp (even free ones) that will work perfectly well for you, it's just a case of establishing what you need in your email marketing strategy.

For users with small subscriber numbers who just want a simple and free solution, Mailchimp is one of the better platforms. However, now that you're no longer able to schedule emails on the free plan or set up automations, and the email templates begin to look very outdated, a free Mailchimp alternative may be a better choice.

If you want quality features with a smaller price tag, it’s worth investigating other companies such as MailerLite, Brevo or Moosend. They are all really good value-for-money email marketing platforms.

However, if you’re a power user, you should really look to ActiveCampaign or GetResponse if you want to create complex automations that react to the way your subscribers behave.

Finally, if you also need a CRM, ActiveCampaign and Zoho are good options.
